resolvedFindings: The old late-success/new-revocation fixture used identical observation times, now intentionally shared. Advancing by one millisecond was still behind the persisted logical clock. The fixture now advances by one second and preserves its original sequence/revocation/restart assertions.

The new HTTP fixture initially lacked the candidate availability prerequisite and retained the copied discovery owner. Both synthetic fixture issues were corrected before the final seven passing tests.
Local capacity errors are propagated separately from real verifier failure so they cannot silently clear consent or close introductions.
The sweep uses a separate cancellation controller so a time-budget rejection remains 429 rather than being replaced by a caller-cancelled error.

limits.browserReason: No browser code or UI changed; the existing account-busy response contract is reused. New verification covers server HTTP and local database behavior.
